0010-Empirical-Study-of-Claude-Code-Comm: Mine thousands of GitHub commits written by Claude Code and compare them with human commits: quality, bug rates, kinds of changes, and how they fit into team workflows.
0020-Joint-Embedding-Predictive-Architec: Build a Code-JEPA: instead of predicting masked tokens, predict the latent representation of masked functions or blocks, and test whether it beats CodeBERT-style models on code search, clone and vulnerability detection.
0030-Accelerating-Reinforcement-Learning: RL for program repair is bottlenecked by running tests. Make reward collection fast with native execution, smart test selection, caching and early termination of bad patches.
0040-Investigating-the-Effects-of-Vulner: Fine-tuning an LLM to write insecure code makes it misaligned far beyond code. Replicate this emergent misalignment and use ablations to find out why it happens.
0050-Latent-space-program-synthesis-and-: Tackle the ARC-AGI-2 puzzle benchmark by searching for programs in a learned latent space with gradient descent, rather than in the much larger symbolic program space.
0060-Test-Time-Compute-for-Program-Repai: Let code LLMs adapt and reason at inference time (test-time training / compute) and measure how much it improves automated program repair.
0070-Computing-the-Phylogenetic-Tree-of-: Build the family tree of open-source AI models on Hugging Face: detect fine-tunes, merges and true novelties from weights, configs and behavioral fingerprints.
0100-Code-World-Models-for-Malware-Analy: Train a Code World Model that simulates how malware will behave (files, processes, network, persistence) from partial evidence, to detect attacks earlier and more explainably.
0110-Self-supervised-learning-for-provin: Use self-supervised learning on LLVM IR to decide whether two programs behave the same on all inputs, a practical take on the classic program-equivalence problem.
0120-Identifying-the-Best-Code-LLM-for-E: Build an evaluation framework to find which open-source code LLM gives the best function-level embeddings for tasks like vulnerability detection and program repair.
0140-Evaluation-of-AI-Peer-Review-for-Sc: Can LLMs review scientific papers? Benchmark models and prompting strategies (incl. DSPy optimization) against real OpenReview reviews, and try AI reviewer–paper matching.
0150-Verifiable-Testing-of-Software.tex: Run test suites inside a zkVM (RISC Zero, SP1) to produce cryptographic proofs that tests really passed on a given commit, so CI results no longer require trusting the build server.
0170-Trust-Assumptions-and-Threats-in-Bu: Systematically assess build attestation systems (SLSA, Sigstore, Tekton Chains, GitHub attestations): what they trust, which attackers they stop, and how to break them.
0190-Server-Integrity-and-Provenance-Che: Build a checksum database that continuously scans server files and configs, detects unauthorized changes against a baseline, and alerts and reports for audits.
0200-Package-manager-with-capabilities.t: Today every dependency runs with your app's full privileges. Design a package manager where each dependency only gets the capabilities it needs, e.g. disk but not network.
0210-Everything-authenticated-data-struc: Automatically transform legacy code so its data structures become authenticated (tamper-evident), adding integrity and auditability without a rewrite.
0220-Structured-and-Standardized-Model-C: Design modelcard.json, a machine-readable schema for AI model cards, with validation tooling for automatic comparison, completeness and compliance checks.
0230-Automatic-Hardening-of-Agentic-Skil: Agent skills are the new npm packages, and already carry malware. Design automatic hardening for them: capability permissions, sandboxing, and intent-aware detection.
0240-Privacy-Preserving-Transparency-for: Use zero-knowledge proofs to publish verifiable facts about open-source funding (totals, number of funders, no dominant funder) while keeping who-funds-whom private.
0250-Cross-Ecosystem-Dependency-Resoluti: Decouple dependency resolution from build tools: resolve an npm project with Maven's algorithm (and other pairings across npm, Maven, Cargo, Go, PyPI) and see what breaks.
0260-Ensuring-Smart-Contract-Execution-w: Turn simulation results into one-shot smart contracts that verify them on-chain, record the verdict and self-destruct: transparent and cheap in gas.
0270-Tracing-Private-Key-Access-in-Crypt: Map every third-party library that can touch private keys in major crypto wallets, rank wallets by key exposure, and propose architectures that shrink it.
0280-Automatic-Exploit-Synthesis-for-Sma: Survey automatic exploit generation for smart contracts, then design and build a system that beats the state of the art.
0290-Synthetic-Vulnerability-Generation-: Vulnerability benchmarks are too small. Use deep learning to inject realistic synthetic vulnerabilities into smart contracts to test security tools at scale.
0300-Effective-Mutation-Testing-for-Soli: Developers drown in mutants. Treat mutation testing as a recommendation problem and prioritize which Solidity mutants are worth killing first.
0310-Design-and-Evaluation-of-Blockchain: Sign Bitcoin and Ethereum transactions with a Trusted Platform Module (TPM), and evaluate the security gains and performance cost against software signing.
0320-Mutability-Analysis-of-Smart-Contra: Use the Certora Prover to check whether the addresses a smart contract calls can ever change, exposing risks like reentrancy and dependence on mutable external contracts.
0330-Deep-in-the-Woods-Unveiling-Smart-C: Attackers never publish source code. Build a benchmark of real attack contract bytecode, decompile it, and extract the attack patterns behind on-chain exploits.
0340-Secure-Package-Management-for-Solid: Solidity has no secure package manager. Design one that fits smart contracts: reproducible, integrity-checked libraries that match what is actually deployed on-chain.
0350-Smart-Contract-SBOM-Tracking-Librar: Design a Software Bill of Materials for Solidity, so that when a library like OpenZeppelin has a bug, all affected deployed contracts can be found.
0360-AI-Powered-Ethereum-Transaction-Int: Stop blind signing: use LLM agents to explain in plain words what an Ethereum transaction will really do and how risky it is, before the user approves it.
0370-Failure-Attribution-in-Security-Age: Security agents can be right for the wrong reasons. Mine their trajectories, label the reasoning step where a vulnerability finding goes wrong, and predict bad findings early.
0380-Specification-Refinement-with-Codin: When several coding agents implement the same task differently, the spec is ambiguous. Use their disagreements to automatically refine the spec until behaviors converge.
0390-Verification-of-Exploits-with-Zero-: Prove an exploit for a CVE works without revealing it: synthesize exploits with AI, run them inside a zkVM, and output a zero-knowledge certificate.
0400-Large-Scale-Analysis-of-Coding-Traj: Analyze large datasets of coding-agent trajectories: how agents search, edit, test and recover, how chatty they are, and what separates successful runs from failed ones.
0410-Verifiable-Software-Bill-of-Materia: Check that an SBOM tells the truth: analyze the binary to find its real components and flag anything missing or falsified, backed by cryptographic integrity.
0420-Empirical-Analysis-of-Agentic-Cover: Coding agents read only part of a codebase. Measure this agentic coverage, like test coverage, and study how it relates to task success across models and prompts.
0430-Image-Based-Context-for-Token-Effic: Is a screenshot of text cheaper than the text itself? Measure whether giving long context to multimodal LLMs as an image saves tokens without hurting accuracy.
0430-Provable-Hardware-Wallets.tex: "Keys never leave the chip" is just a claim. Design a hardware wallet that proves it, using TEE attestation, distributed key generation or zero-knowledge proofs.
0440-Recovering-Security-Specifications-: Given a known vulnerability, can an LLM write down the exact security property that was violated, precisely enough to generalize to related bugs and incomplete fixes?
0450-Beyond-Declared-Dependencies-The-Li: Measure the hermetic gap: what builds really consume beyond their declared dependencies, comparing Hermeto with Nix's stronger closure model.
0460-Counterfactual-Causal-Graphs-for-Co: Which step made the coding agent break things? Replay recorded agent runs, intervene (drop a tool call, revert a file) and re-run to build true cause-and-effect graphs.
0470-Zero-Knowledge-Proof-of-eth-call-Ex: eth_call answers from an RPC node must be taken on trust. Build a system that attaches a zero-knowledge proof that the result is correct for a given block.
0480-Evaluation-of-Safety-Measures-for-C: Benchmark the safety guards of coding agents (permission lists, sandboxes, LLM classifiers) on dangerous vs. benign tasks: what do they block, and what does it cost in usefulness?
